newsitem.title: USA: Cash flows into U.S. stock funds reverse - survey.
newsitem.headline: Cash flows into U.S. stock funds reverse - survey.

text.p: Cash flows into U.S. stock mutual funds reversed to inflows of $1.05 billion for the three days ended January 30 from outflows of $710 million for the two-day period ended January 27, according to a survey of funds followed by Mutual Fund Trim Tabs.
International funds posted inflows of $407 million for the three-day period versus outflows of $265 million for the prior two days, according to the fund tracking firm.

Aggressive growth funds recorded inflows of $432 million versus outflows of $576 million, growth had inflows of $250 million versus outflows of $273 million, and growth and income had inflows of $427 million versus inflows of $194 million.

Bond funds recorded inflows of $22 million versus outflows of $116 million, according to the firm. Muni funds posted inflows of $11 million versus outflows of $195 million, and corporate/income/global funds also reversed, with inflows of $18 million versus outflows of $24 million. Government/GNMA funds recorded a jump in outflows to $120 million from $3 million.
